---
title: FAQ and troubleshooting
description: Common errors with their exit codes and fixes, how to recover from an invalid mcpgen.json, and how to upgrade mcpgen.
---

## Frequently asked questions

**Is generation deterministic?** Yes. Same `mcpgen.json` in, same project out. Golden tests in `internal/generator/testdata/golden` pin the output byte-for-byte.

**Can I edit generated files?** User-owned files (handlers, prompts, resources, tests): always. mcpgen-owned files: you can, but the next regen skips them with `modified since generation (hash mismatch)` — your edit wins. Never edit inside `// mcpgen:begin/end` marker regions; `add` then exits 5 until you restore them.

**How do I remove a tool/prompt/resource?** Delete its entry from `mcpgen.json`, delete its user-owned files first, then `mcpgen new <dir> --force --no-check`. See [add capabilities](/mcpgen/guides/add-capabilities/).

**Why is the conformance stage skipped?** It runs only when node/npx are present, transport is `http`, and protocol is `compat`. stdio has no HTTP endpoint; `latest-only` rejects the suite's legacy handshake by design. Force it with `--conformance` (fails with exit 6 if node/npx are missing).

**What does "8/30 checks passed" mean?** The suite's protocol-level scenarios gate; fixture scenarios that need well-known test tools are reported as non-gating. See [check and conformance](/mcpgen/concepts/check-and-conformance/).

**Is the HTTP server authenticated?** No. It binds to `127.0.0.1` and rejects cross-site `Origin` headers (403). Enable the `oauth` feature and wire `oauthex.RequireAuth` before exposing it on a network. See [security model](/mcpgen/concepts/security-model/).

## Troubleshooting (verified error shapes)

**`DIR_EXISTS` — exit 3.** The target directory exists and is not empty, and you did not pass `--force`:

```json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "code": "DIR_EXISTS",
  "message": "target directory ./weather exists and is not empty",
  "fix": "pass --force to regenerate an existing mcpgen project ...", "exit_code": 3 } }
```

Fix: pass `--force` to regenerate, or choose a new directory.

**`NOT_MCPGEN_PROJECT` — exit 3.** `mcpgen check ./somewhere` where `somewhere` has no `mcpgen.json` / `.mcpgen/manifest.json`. Fix: run from a generated project root, or create one with `mcpgen new`.

**`CONFIG_INVALID` — exit 2.** `mcpgen.json` failed validation. The message lists every problem, for example an id that violates `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`, a duplicate id, a bad transport, or a port outside 1-65535. Fix: edit `mcpgen.json`; `error.fix` points at the file. Recover by fixing the fields, or — if the file is beyond repair — regenerate the project with `mcpgen new <dir> --force --no-check` after backing up your user-owned files, which regen never touches.

**`CONFIG_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` — exit 2.** Only `"version": 1` is supported by mcpgen v1. Fix: set `"version": 1` or regenerate.

**`CONFLICT` — exit 5.** Duplicate id in `mcpgen.json`, id already in a marker region, or markers missing/unparseable in a registration file. Fix: choose a different id, or restore the `// mcpgen:begin <region>` / `// mcpgen:end <region>` markers (regen with `--force` recreates the registration files only if they are unmodified — delete a damaged one first and regen recreates it).

**`PREREQUISITE_MISSING` — exit 6.** The Go toolchain is not on `PATH` (every pipeline stops here), or `--conformance` was forced without node/npx. Fix: install Go 1.26+ or Node.js, or drop the flag.

**`SPEC_INVALID` — exit 2.** The spec file passed to `add` is unreadable or invalid (bad id pattern, bad JSON). Nothing is written. Fix the spec.

**A stage failed in `check` (exit 1).** Read `error.stage`, `error.code`, and `error.fix` — `fix` names the first failure with its `file:line`, for example `first failure: TestGreet (greet_test.go:30); run 'go test -race ./...' in ./weather`. Fix, re-run `mcpgen check ./weather --json`.

## Upgrade mcpgen

```sh
go install github.com/alesr/mcpgen@latest     # or download a release binary
mcpgen version                                  # check what you run
```

Generated files carry the generator version in their header (`// Code generated by mcpgen vX.Y.Z. DO NOT EDIT.`) and in `.mcpgen/manifest.json`. After upgrading, regenerate with `mcpgen new <dir> --force --no-check` to bring mcpgen-owned files up to date; user-owned files and modified mcpgen-owned files are skipped as always. The `tidy` stage of `check` also verifies the generated project still pins `go-sdk v1.8.0` — if you hand-downgrade the pin, `check` fails and tells you to restore it or regen.
